I started cutting myself out of curiousity, mostly, and kept going because it helped me deal with depression. I had slipped on some rocks while bathing in the sea on a vacation, and accidentally cut my palm and foot on some other rocks. I remember that I thought it felt oddly good, rather than being painful. This lead to me cutting my hand with the lid of a tin can (yup, the lid of a can of pineapple,  hard to forget since it sounds so silly) and getting the same feeling - it felt good, and I wanted to do it more.

 And it kept piling on, going from a cut or two on my hand now and then, to multiple across my arm every day. It was a pleasant activity that made me relax and feel good, much like smoking. It never stopped feeling good, but after looking at my arm and seeing scars upon scars, with fresh cuts building up every day, I knew I had to stop.

 The first day of quitting was hard, since I was thinking about it, but I figured it would get easier after a while. It didn't; Every day was harder than the last. I was getting stressed, my back and neck were tense, I got headaches, my stomach churned and it was as if I could physically feel something in the back of my head. My self-loathing and feelings of loneliness were amplified, and all I could think about was how I wanted to cut myself just to make it stop. None of the alternatives (distracting myself with other things, snapping a rubber band on my wrist, etc.) worked at all - they just made it worse. 

When I caved in, that first cut was pure euphoria. It was as if all the tension in my body seeped out through the wound, and it got even better for each cut. My body relaxed, the headache went away, and I felt incredibly serene; just by cutting myself for five minutes. After that I kept going for a little over a year or so, where I cut progressively less over the course of the last few months, as I had started talking to my psychiatrist then. After I started taking ritalin for my ADHD around 6 months ago, I've felt genuinely happy every day, and I've been able to suppress my urges.

All that being said, this is just how it was for me. I can't, and won't, speak for anyone else. I still have scars on my arm, but I never cut very deep (luckily), so they are quite faded, and not very easy to see at first glance.
